Proximal Operator of a Penalty

Source: R/prox.R
penalty_prox.Rd

Returns the point that minimizes the penalty plus a quadratic pull towards \(v\),

$$\mathrm{prox}_{t\rho}(v) = \arg\min_{\beta} \left\{ \tfrac{1}{2t}\lVert \beta - v \rVert^{2} + \rho(\beta;\theta) \right\},$$

A proximal gradient method applies the operator after each gradient step. With it, a penalty with a kink is minimized without differentiating it at the kink, and a coefficient can be set exactly to zero, where a gradient method only brings it close to zero.

Usage

penalty_prox(pen, v, step, theta, ...)

Arguments

pen

A penalty() object. has_prox() tests whether it has an operator.

v

A numeric vector of length pen@n_coef, the point of the quadratic pull. The vector is coerced with as.numeric().

step

The step length \(t\), a single positive finite number. A vector is rejected; penalty_prox_spec() takes one step per coefficient.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector, holding every name in pen@params, each a single number.

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not use it.

Value

A numeric vector of the same length as v.

The operator of each branch

branchoperator
quadratic, structuredone linear solve, \((I + tS)^{-1}v\), with \(S\) the penalty's Hessian
Gaussian prior centered at zerothe shrinkage \(v/(1 + t/\sigma^2)\)
Laplace priorthe soft threshold \(\mathrm{sign}(v)(\lvert v\rvert - t\lambda)_{+}\)
elastic netthe soft threshold at \(t\lambda\alpha\), followed by division by \(1 + t\lambda(1-\alpha)\)
SCAD, MCPthe piecewise operators of Fan and Li (2001) and Zhang (2010)
any other separable parentthe stationary point of smallest objective, coordinate by coordinate

Each closed form is the minimizer of the defining objective, and the page of each method gives its formula.

The stationary condition, where there is no closed form

A separable penalty whose parent has a differentiable log-density, and which is not one of the closed-form families, is solved coordinate by coordinate from the stationary condition

$$\frac{\beta - v}{t} = \ell^{(y)}(\beta),$$

whose right-hand side is distributions7::distrib_grad_y(). For a density that is not log-concave, such as the Student t of heavy_penalty(), the condition can have more than one root, and the operator is the root of smallest objective. The segment between \(v\) and the mode of the parent is scanned for changes of sign, each change is refined by uniroot() to a relative accuracy of about eps^0.75, and the candidate of smallest objective is returned. For a unimodal parent the global minimizer lies on that segment, so the value returned is the global minimizer. For a parent with more than one mode, the value returned is a stationary point that need not be the global minimizer; .prox_root() gives the details. A parent that declares a kink and is not one of the closed-form families is rejected, because the stationary condition does not hold at a kink and the minimizer of such a penalty can lie there.

Under a map

The quadratic branch takes any map, because the objective stays quadratic, and a structured penalty has no map. The separable, SCAD and MCP branches need the identity map or a diagonal one. Under a diagonal map with entries \(d_j\), the operator is the operator without the map evaluated at \(d_j v_j\) with the step \(t d_j^2\), and then divided by \(d_j\); in this way the standardization of a column enters the operator. A general \(D\) mixes the coordinates and turns the problem into the generalized-lasso problem, which requires an algorithm of its own, so such a penalty is rejected with a message naming it. A diagonal map is recognized by its Matrix class, as map_diagonal() describes.

Calls that signal an error

  • a penalty with no operator, such as an additive_penalty(), with a message naming has_prox();

  • a separable, SCAD or MCP penalty under a map that is not a Matrix diagonal object with nonzero entries;

  • a separable penalty whose parent is read in blocks, because the coordinates of a block do not separate;

  • a Laplace or elastic-net parent that is not centered at zero, because the closed form is written for a parent centered at zero;

  • a separable parent that declares a kink and has no closed form;

  • a stationary condition that changes sign neither on the segment between \(v\) and the mode of the parent nor in a widened bracket;

  • SCAD where \(t c_j \ge a - 1\) and MCP where \(t c_j \ge \gamma\) in some coordinate, where \(c_j\) is the curvature curv of the penalty and \(t\) is multiplied by \(d_j^2\) under a diagonal map; the subproblem is then not convex and the operator is set-valued;

  • a step that is not a single positive finite number, or a v whose length is not pen@n_coef.

Methods

The method on the base class penalty() signals an error naming the penalty and pointing to has_prox(); AdditivePenalty() inherits it. The classes with an operator of their own are:

  • one linear solve;

  • StructuredPenalty(): penalty_prox(), the same linear solve;

  • a closed form for the Gaussian, Laplace and elastic-net parents and the stationary point of smallest objective for any other parent;

  • ScadPenalty(): penalty_prox(), the piecewise operator of Fan and Li (2001);

  • McpPenalty(): penalty_prox(), the piecewise operator of Zhang (2010).

References

Fan, J. and Li, R. (2001). Variable selection via nonconcave penalized likelihood and its oracle properties. Journal of the American Statistical Association 96, 1348-1360.

Zhang, C.-H. (2010). Nearly unbiased variable selection under minimax concave penalty. Annals of Statistics 38, 894-942.

See also

has_prox() to test whether a penalty has an operator, penalty_prox_spec() for the same operator as a table that a compiled loop can read, penalty_kinks() for the points where a gradient method fails, penalty_gradient() for the gradient where the penalty is smooth.

Examples

v <- c(2, 0.3, -1.4)

# The lasso: a soft threshold, so the middle coordinate becomes exactly 0.
penalty_prox(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3), v, 1, list(lambda = 1))
#> [1]  1.0  0.0 -0.4

# A ridge: a shrinkage towards zero, which sets no coordinate to zero.
penalty_prox(ridge_penalty(n_coef = 3), v, 1, list(lambda = 1.5))
#> [1]  0.80  0.12 -0.56
v / (1 + 1 * 1.5)
#> [1]  0.80  0.12 -0.56

# The elastic net applies the soft threshold and then the shrinkage.
penalty_prox(elasticnet_penalty(n_coef = 3), v, 1,
             list(lambda = 1, alpha = 0.6))
#> [1]  1.0000000  0.0000000 -0.5714286

# A heavy-tailed prior has no closed form, so the operator is found from
# the stationary condition. With sigma = 1, nu = 4 and step 1 it maps 2 to
# 1, as the ridge with lambda = 1 does, and it moves the coordinate 10 much
# less than that ridge does.
v2 <- c(2, 0.3, 10)
penalty_prox(heavy_penalty(n_coef = 3), v2, 1, list(sigma = 1, nu = 4))
#> [1] 1.0000000 0.1336635 9.4958181
penalty_prox(ridge_penalty(n_coef = 3), v2, 1, list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] 1.00 0.15 5.00

# Each operator minimizes the defining objective. The next call finds the
# minimizer for the first coordinate of the lasso.
rho <- lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3)
obj <- function(b1) {
  x <- v; x[1] <- b1
  0.5 * sum((x - v)^2) / 1 + penalty_value(rho, x, list(lambda = 1))
}
stats::optimize(obj, c(-5, 5), tol = 1e-12)$minimum
#> [1] 1

# An additive penalty has no operator, and the call signals an error.
try(penalty_prox(additive_penalty(list(diag(3), diag(c(1, 1, 0)))),
                 v, 1, list(lambda1 = 1, lambda2 = 1)))
#> Error : 'additive [2 components]' has no proximal operator.
#>   A penalty has one when it is a quadratic or structured penalty, a SCAD
#>   or MCP penalty, or a separable penalty under the identity map or a
#>   diagonal map. has_prox() tests this before a call.
